title: Count a card's purchases only when they go through

blocks.text: The fraud team has a velocity rule: no card gets more than three purchases a day through this server, and the fourth is refused with `65`. `VelocityLimit` enforces it, in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/VelocityLimit.java`, ahead of the authorizer. The daily counts are given (`DailyCounts`), and so is the refusal (`tooMany`).

Finish `prepare` and `abort`, marked `TODO`. A purchase counts only if it goes through: one the authorizer declines must not use up the card's day, and once a card has had its three, every further purchase that day is refused. About 15 lines in total.
The tests deploy a real TransactionManager with Q2, in the test's own JVM, with the real `SendResponse` after the authorizer.

cases.says: an approved purchase is answered 00 and counts once for its card
a card that has had its purchases for the day is refused with 65, and the refusal is answered
a purchase a later participant declines is given back, because the participant that counted it joined and hears the abort
the participant's own refusal counted nothing, so its abort, if it gets one, gives nothing back

origin.section: 4.2 A Participant Hears the Outcome Only If It Joined

concepts: Only participants that joined get commit or abort; one that changed something outside the Context in prepare must join and undo it in abort, and one that votes ABORTED joins too unless it says NO_JOIN.
